title: [P0] User-facing latency SLO breach — multi-service degradation

failure.root_cause_statement: session-db PostgreSQL connection timeout was silently changed from 30s to 300s via a config management drift 6 hours ago, causing user-service to hold idle connections open 10x longer than expected, exhausting the connection pool and creating a queue of waiting requests that manifests as latency spikes and eventual 503s for all user-facing endpoints

red_herrings.description: analytics-collector is running its daily aggregation pipeline, consuming high CPU and producing alarming log volume — it has no upstream user impact and is completely isolated from the connection pool issue
profile-service shows elevated error rate because user-service is too slow to provide user context that profile-service depends on — it is a cascading victim

api-gateway recently had its access log verbosity increased from INFO to DEBUG for a brief audit window — this produces 10x more log volume making it appear far more active than usual and distracts from the real signal

title: [P1] Product API latency explosion after deployment rollout

failure.root_cause_statement: a rolling restart of product-api during deployment flushed all local in-process caches simultaneously, causing every instance to stampede cache-cluster on cold start, and when cache-cluster itself began evicting under load all instances fell through to product-db concurrently, amplifying DB queries 200x and causing a sustained overload cascade

red_herrings.description: price-service shows timeout errors because product-api is too slow to forward pricing context — price-service itself is idle and healthy but its SLO dashboard lights up red making it appear broken
image-cdn origin pull rate spikes because product-api cache misses cause more image metadata fetches than normal — it looks like an image infrastructure problem but is a downstream symptom

title: [P1] Reporting API queries running 50x slower after maintenance window

failure.root_cause_statement: schema-migration-runner dropped an index named idx_events_user_created_at during a maintenance window believing it to be a duplicate, but this index was the primary access path for the most common reporting query pattern, causing full sequential table scans on a 2-billion-row table and query times to spike from 80ms to 45+ seconds

title: [P0] Platform-wide latency storm — all services degraded simultaneously

failure.root_cause_statement: a CDN cache purge accompanying the v12.0.0 deploy invalidated all 28 million cached objects simultaneously, causing 100% of traffic to miss CDN and hit edge-api as cold requests concurrently, which overwhelmed session-service and content-service causing them to hammer origin-db with un-cached queries at 400x normal volume

red_herrings.description: personalisation-engine shows extreme CPU and timeout errors because content-service is too slow to provide content objects for personalisation — its ML model is fine but it cannot process requests without content objects

session-service appears to be the primary bottleneck because it is responding slowest and causing the most visible errors — but it is equally a victim of the cache purge storm as content-service, and focusing on session-service distracts from the CDN root cause

edge-api shows massive request rate spike that looks like a traffic attack or DDoS — request rate jumps 40x which matches an attack pattern, but it is entirely due to CDN cache misses routing to origin

title: [P0] Complete service mesh freeze — all requests hanging indefinitely

failure.root_cause_statement: a distributed lock contention created a circular wait: service-a holds lock L1 and waits for lock L2, service-b holds lock L2 and waits for lock L3, service-c holds lock L3 and waits for lock L1, creating a system-wide deadlock that causes all three services to hang indefinitely since lock-manager has no deadlock detection timeout configured

red_herrings.description: circuit-breaker-proxy opens all circuit breakers after 30 seconds of upstream timeouts, producing a cascade of CIRCUIT_OPEN alerts that make it appear the services themselves are crashing or overloaded when they are actually deadlocked waiting for locks

api-router shows 100% request timeout rate and logs suggest it is dropping all connections, making it look like the router is misconfigured or overloaded — it is healthy but all requests hang waiting for the deadlocked services

service-b is the most visible hung service because it sits in the middle of the dependency chain and both service-a and service-c reference it in their timeout logs — but all three services are equally deadlocked

title: [P1] Database writes failing — ENOSPC on all insert/update operations
causal_chain: wal-archiver: archive cleanup cron has been failing due to permission error for 5 days (root)
wal-archive-volume: fills to 100%, archiver pauses, WAL accumulates locally on postgres-primary
postgres-primary: pg_wal directory fills, PostgreSQL enters read-only mode with ENOSPC
write-api: symptom — all writes failing, reads still working, confusing split behavior

failure.root_cause_statement: wal-archiver archive cleanup cron job has been failing silently for 5 days due to a permissions error on /archive/old/, causing the archive volume to fill to 100%, which paused WAL archiving, causing WAL segments to accumulate on postgres-primary until its pg_wal directory also filled, triggering PostgreSQL read-only mode and failing all write operations

red_herrings.description: read-api shows elevated latency and occasional errors because PostgreSQL performs emergency checkpoints under disk pressure, stalling read query planning — reads are partially affected but not the problem
write-api error logs are the most prominent and look like a write-api application bug or connection pool issue — the ENOSPC message buried in postgres logs is the real signal, not the write-api code

failure.root_cause_statement: bgp-speaker accepted a route update from a peering neighbor that created asymmetric routing — outbound packets from search-service to index-builder traverse a different path than return packets, crossing a stateful firewall that drops the untracked return flow with TCP RST

cdn-origin reports increased origin pulls because edge caches are timing out on search results and falling back to origin, creating a spike in origin traffic that looks like a CDN misconfiguration
telemetry-collector shows gaps in metrics collection from index-builder, which looks like an instrumentation bug rather than a network routing issue

title: [P1] Increasing GC pauses and request timeouts — JVM service degradation

failure.root_cause_statement: classloader-agent dynamically compiles and loads Groovy rule classes on every rule update without releasing old classloaders, filling JVM metaspace on the data-enrichment service where it runs as an embedded agent, causing full GC storms that freeze the service for seconds at a time

red_herrings.description: ml-scorer shows elevated latency because rule-engine is slow to send scoring requests, creating a backlog that makes ml-scorer appear overloaded
event-bus shows consumer lag growing because both rule-engine and data-enrichment are slow to consume events, which looks like an event bus throughput issue
monitoring-proxy reports metric collection timeouts from data-enrichment during GC pauses, appearing as a monitoring infrastructure problem

title: [P0] Leader election instability and distributed consensus failures across clusters

failure.root_cause_statement: tsc-firmware applied a CPU microcode update on consensus-service hosts that altered TSC frequency calibration, causing time.Now() to drift by 200-400ms per minute relative to wall clock, which breaks the distributed consensus protocol's lease timeout detection and triggers continuous leader re-elections

red_herrings.description: state-store shows write conflicts and lock contention because consensus-service keeps changing leaders mid-transaction, making it appear as a storage layer consistency problem
cache-proxy hit rate drops because api-gateway circuit-breaks consensus paths and retries through cache, flooding it with uncacheable consensus-dependent requests
health-monitor flags consensus-service nodes as flapping between healthy/unhealthy states, which looks like a monitoring false positive rather than real instability

title: [P0] Cascading timeouts from latency-sensitive service — multi-tier degradation

failure.root_cause_statement: numa-balancer kernel thread migrated the matching-engine process from NUMA node 0 to NUMA node 1 during a load spike, causing all memory accesses to cross the QPI interconnect with 3x latency (40ns to 120ns), pushing the latency-sensitive matching loop from sub-millisecond to multi-millisecond response times and triggering cascading timeouts in all upstream consumers

red_herrings.description: order-book shows increased lock contention because matching-engine is slow to release order locks, creating a backlog that appears to be a storage bottleneck
market-data feed latency increases because matching-engine is slow to consume ticks, causing the feed buffer to fill and drop messages, appearing as a data provider issue
session-cache eviction rate spikes because api-tier holds sessions longer during timeouts, filling the cache and triggering LRU evictions that look like a cache sizing problem

title: [P0] TLS handshake storm — connection establishment failures across fleet

failure.root_cause_statement: ticket-rotator failed to distribute new TLS session ticket encryption keys to the tls-terminator fleet before the old keys expired, causing all clients attempting session resumption to fail, forcing full TLS handshakes that overwhelm the tls-terminator CPU capacity and create a connection establishment bottleneck

red_herrings.description: cdn-edge shows origin connection failures because tls-terminator is refusing new connections under load, making it appear as a CDN origin configuration issue
webhook-relay shows delivery failures because api-service is too slow to accept webhook posts during the connection storm, appearing as a webhook infrastructure problem
log-shipper shows elevated CPU from processing the surge of TLS error logs from tls-terminator, making it look like a log pipeline bottleneck that is contributing to the problem

title: [P1] Dual service degradation — unexplained latency on colocated workloads

failure.root_cause_statement: page-cache-mgr kernel memory management allowed indexer-service and analytics-engine (colocated on the same physical host) to compete for page cache, with analytics-engine's sequential scan pattern evicting indexer-service's random-access mmap'd index files, causing both services to degrade as they continuously re-fault pages from disk

red_herrings.description: document-store shows increased read latency because indexer-service is issuing more reads as its cached index pages get evicted, appearing as a storage backend problem
recommendation-svc latency increases because both search-api and analytics-engine are slow, making it look like a recommendation algorithm performance regression
job-scheduler recently launched a batch compaction job on the same host that coincides with the degradation timeline, appearing as the trigger when it is actually unrelated
